title: Typhoid Fever
subtitle: A serious and potentially fatal bacterial infection caused by Salmonella typhi, spread through contaminated food and water. Particularly common in areas with poor sanitation.

sections.title: Symptoms
sections.intro: Typhoid fever remains a serious public health problem in many parts of Asia, Africa, and Latin America. Early antibiotic treatment is essential to prevent complications.
items: Gradually rising fever reaching 40°C (104°F)
Weakness and fatigue
Stomach pain, headache, and loss of appetite
Diarrhea or constipation
Rose-colored spots on chest and abdomen
Enlarged spleen and liver

sections.title: Causes
sections.intro: Typhoid fever is caused by the bacterium Salmonella enterica serovar Typhi (S. typhi). It is exclusively a human pathogen.
items: Salmonella typhi bacterium in contaminated water or food
Spread by poor hand hygiene, fecal-oral route
Contaminated drinking water from sewage
Raw fruits, vegetables washed in contaminated water

sections.title: Prevention
items: Typhoid vaccine, oral and injectable options available
Drink only bottled or boiled water
Eat food that is thoroughly cooked and still hot
Wash hands with soap before eating and after toilet use
Avoid raw vegetables and salads in high risk areas
Proper sanitation and sewage treatment

sections.title: Treatment
items: Antibiotics: Ciprofloxacin, Azithromycin, or Ceftriaxone
Dexamethasone for severe cases with neurological complications
Rest and stay well hydrated
Oral rehydration for diarrhea management
Surgery may be needed for intestinal perforation
Carriers should be treated to prevent ongoing spread

facts: South Asia, Sub-Saharan Africa, South-East Asia
